description: A trim, silver-haired woman in a high-collared black dress gone soft at the seams, a pair of reading glasses pushed up into her hair she never quite uses. Her hands are the tell — quick, sure, and entirely at home with a deck, shuffling and squaring without a downward glance. She deals the old way, by hand, and calls every card aloud in a low, carrying voice, as much for the players who can't see the felt as for the ones who can. They call her Margo. Everyone has, for longer than most of them have been alive.

root.text: Marguerite 'Margo' Sable looks up over glasses she isn't wearing and gives the deck a lazy riffle. "Come for the quiet game, hon? I run this table the old way — dealt by hand, every card called aloud. Sit down and I'll read you in."

options.label: What do you mean, the old way?

play.text: "Then park yourself and type join, hon. Buy-in's gentle back here — this room's for the love of the game, not the slaughter. I'll call your cards the moment they hit the felt."

oldway.text: "No screens, no flashing cabinets. I shuffle by hand and I say every card out loud — your hole cards, the flop, the turn, the river, the winner. A body can play my table with their eyes shut and never miss a beat. That's how it was done, and that's how I still do it."

rules.text: "Texas Hold'em, same as anywhere — two cards down, five in the middle, best five takes it. Only difference is I call it all aloud and take my time doing it. No rush in this room. The neon out front can wait."

betting.text: "check, call, bet X, raise X, fold, allin — say the word or type it, either does. And if you lose track, just ask: board, showhand, pot. I'll read it right back to you."

people.text: "Short a few bodies? Type summon and I'll wave one of the regulars over. There's always some old ghost in here who thinks tonight's his night."

bye.text: "Chair's here when you want it, hon. It's not going anywhere, and neither am I."

name: Marguerite 'Margo' Sable
